activation.note: Activation covers new and existing issue bodies with Dependencies-section #N entries, including review and validation, and excludes references outside that section. Task terms are explicitly hints rather than prerequisites; artifact, operation, and finding observation requirements are acknowledged.

audit.summary: All source segments survive at the claimed destinations, with the classification requirement and trailing-marker definition available to the coder and enforcement metadata retained for verification and audit. Additional tag-selection guidance, remediation guidance, and the anti-gaming instruction are explicitly declared; there are no added waivers or application-specific restrictions.

segmentChecks.note: The given/when/then fields preserve the full scope: every #N entry in an issue body's Dependencies section must have exactly one of the four allowed tags. The activation and avoid fields reinforce rather than narrow that obligation.
The why field retains the rationale verbatim, including prevention of the session-template merge-wait loop hanging on sibling or parallel work.
The dependency_entry definition is retained in verifier_detail and operationally in given and activation, including the restriction to the Dependencies section.
Then and verifier_detail preserve both the trailing-marker requirement and the closed prereq/merged/sibling/parallel vocabulary.
The validator type and complete test reference remain in audit; evidence also exposes the validator's short name for verification.
Verifier_detail and audit preserve the exact 2026-12-31 suppression deadline and state that suppressions are allowed only until then.

risks: No concrete serialized entry example or delimiter syntax is supplied, so a weak planner knows the marker must be trailing but not whether to write forms such as '#N prereq', '#N (prereq)', or '#N — prereq'. The canonical source also leaves this syntax unspecified.

unobservable: file_kind=issue_body requires a new observer because issue bodies are tracker content rather than repository files.
operation=create/edit/review/validate requires a new observer for the tracker/workflow operation.
finding=test_issue_deps_have_classification_tags requires a new observer to expose validator findings.

No currently observable structured fact is declared for parsing the Dependencies section, its #N entries, or each entry's trailing marker; an issue-body parser/observer must supply these before a Datalog engine can evaluate the content condition.

review.summary: The sampled statement, rationale, definitions, validator reference, and deadline are all preserved, and the coder-facing fields make the classification decision clear apart from unspecified marker formatting. Activation is semantically well scoped but not presently executable by Datalog without the explicitly acknowledged tracker, operation, finding, and issue-body parsing observers. I agree with the auditor's PASS verdict.
